details.description: o1 is OpenAI's first full o-series reasoning model, trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to work through a long internal chain of thought before answering. The current snapshot, o1-2024-12-17, was released December 17, 2024, accepts text and image input, produces text output, and offers a 200,000-token context window with up to 100,000 output tokens. OpenAI's own model catalog now labels it a 'Previous full o-series reasoning model' and marks the snapshot deprecated; Microsoft's Azure retirement schedule lists a retirement date of November 19, 2026, with gpt-5.6-sol as the recommended replacement.
advantages: Accepts image input alongside text, letting it reason over visual inputs for tasks such as diagrams, charts or photos (OpenAI o1 model docs).
Supports streaming, function calling and structured outputs via the Chat Completions and Responses APIs (OpenAI o1 model docs).
Offers a 200,000-token context window with up to 100,000 output tokens, the largest of the original o1-series snapshots (OpenAI o1 model docs).
disadvantages: OpenAI's own model catalog marks this snapshot deprecated and labels it a 'Previous full o-series reasoning model', with gpt-5.6-sol as the suggested replacement.
Knowledge cutoff of October 1, 2023 (OpenAI o1 model docs).
Does not support fine-tuning or predicted outputs (OpenAI o1 model docs).
OpenAI's own documentation rates its response speed as the slowest among current models (OpenAI o1 model docs).
use_cases: Complex multi-step reasoning in science, coding and mathematics
Problem-solving tasks that benefit from an internal chain of thought before answering
Visual reasoning tasks combining text and image input

sources.title: Model retirement schedule - Microsoft Foundry | Microsoft Learn

notes: Bud serves this model only via Azure (azure/eu and azure/us o1-2024-12-17), so Azure's own retirement schedule was used to confirm status: it lists o1 (2024-12-17) as 'Deprecated' with a 2026-11-19 retirement date, exactly matching the catalog's deprecation_date fact. OpenAI's direct-API deprecations page separately lists an earlier 2026-10-23 shutdown date for the same snapshot on OpenAI's own API (not Azure) -- the two hosts run different retirement timelines for the same model, and the catalog's date matches Azure's, which is the relevant host here. No accuracy-style benchmark was found on an opened maker or leaderboard page for this exact snapshot, so evaluations is left empty rather than guessed.
